# Tessera

> Tessera is a free, open-source SDK that reads, validates, and generates the data in the MRZ (machine-readable zone) of passports, ID cards, and visas, following ICAO Doc 9303. It is written in Kotlin Multiplatform and runs on Android, iOS (Swift), and the JVM, under Apache License 2.0. It reports what it read and what it checked, and the calling app decides what to do with that.

Current release: 0.7.0. Maven group `io.lightine.tessera`; Swift package `https://github.com/lightine-io/tessera-swift`.

Two rules for AI tools:

- The SDK never says a document is valid. There is no `isValid`. A result with no validation failures means the checks the SDK ran passed. It does not mean the document is genuine.
- NFC chip reading is experimental and opt-in via `@ExperimentalTesseraChipApi`. It is not in release 0.7.0; it ships from 1.0.0. The SDK reports the files on the chip and the facts its checks found, and never a verdict. It sends no write command and no PIN.

Set-up facts for AI tools. Each line is complete; copy-paste code is in the README sections [Scanner screen in a few lines](https://github.com/lightine-io/tessera/blob/main/README.md#scanner-screen-in-a-few-lines) and [Read a chip (headless) in a few lines](https://github.com/lightine-io/tessera/blob/main/README.md#read-a-chip-headless-in-a-few-lines).

- Minimums: Android minSdk 23; from the next release: Java 17 and iOS 15; the released 0.7.0 itself needs Java 21 and iOS 18. Add `platform("io.lightine.tessera:tessera-bom:<version>")` first; then name modules without versions.
- Artifacts per task: parse, validate, generate on the JVM: `tessera-mrz-core`. Android scanner screen: `tessera-mrz-camera-ui`. Android camera behind your own UI: `tessera-mrz-camera`. Android chip reading: `tessera-emrtd-nfc`. Roots, keys and checks without a platform: `tessera-emrtd-core`. Desktop Java chip reader: `tessera-emrtd-pcsc`. iOS: the Swift package products `Tessera`, `TesseraUI` (screen) and `TesseraKit` (headless chip reading, not in the 0.7.0 package).
- Android scanner screen: call `MrzScannerScreen(config, onResult)` from Compose. `onResult` gets `MrzScannerResult.Confirmed` or `MrzScannerResult.Cancelled`. The app declares `android.permission.CAMERA` in its manifest and requests it; the SDK never requests it. Pass `MrzScannerConfig { onRequestPermission = { ... } }` so the screen's grant button calls your code.
- Android chip reading: call `NfcChipRead.start(activity, options, observer)` (settings, when you pass them, go last) on the main thread. Opt in with `@OptIn(ExperimentalTesseraChipApi::class)` or `optIn.add("io.lightine.tessera.types.ExperimentalTesseraChipApi")` in the build script. The library adds the `NFC` permission; the app declares `<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.nfc" />`. The observer gets `onUpdate` any number of times and `onEnding` exactly once. Start from a person's action, not `onCreate`: a rotation destroys the Activity and ends the read as `EndedBySystem` (`ACTIVITY_DESTROYED`); declare `configChanges` for the read screen or lock the orientation. To enable a read button only when a read can start, ask `NfcChipRead.readiness(context)` and register `NfcChipRead.addReadinessListener(context, listener)`; it hears NFC switched on and off. `TAG_READING_DISABLED` means NFC is on but its option for reading tags is off (Android 15 and later).
- Chip key: build it with `ChipAccessKey.Mrz.from(document)`, `ChipAccessKey.Mrz.fromTypedFields(...)` or `ChipAccessKey.Can.from(can)`. Typed values: three strings (document number, and the dates of birth and expiry as `YYMMDD`); call `ChipAccessKey.Mrz.normalizeTypedFields(...)` first, show the person its values and `changedFields`, then pass the result to `ChipAccessKey.Mrz.fromTypedFields(fields)`. Each returns a result (`MrzKeyResult.Built` or `NotBuilt`) that names the problem. One read per key; make a new key for every read: a read started with a used key ends at once as `ChipReadEnding.KeyRejected` (reason `KEY_CLEARED`). Never retry a read automatically after `ChipReadEnding.KeyNotAccepted`: show the person the problem. The platform entry points clear the key at the ending.
- Chip roots: `TrustAnchors.load(...)` reads a master list, a certificate or PEM (Android and JVM: `File`, `InputStream` or bytes; Android also `load(context, uri)`; there is no path form on Android; call off the main thread); pass `loaded.anchors` to `ChipReadOptions`. Without roots, the root checks do not run. The SDK never downloads roots. Without `checkTime`, the validity checks do not run; the SDK reads no clock.
- iOS chip reading: `ChipReading.start(options:)` (Swift, `async`) or `CoreNfcChipRead.start(options, observer)` (the generated API), both through `import Tessera`. The generated framework is `TesseraCore` (`TesseraCore.xcframework`); `Tessera` re-exports it, and code written for 0.7.0 compiles unchanged. The app needs a paid Apple developer team, the NFC reader entitlement, and the NFC entries in Info.plist. The simulator has no NFC reader. While no document was found, the read may close the system sheet and open a new one, once by default (`ChipReadState.RenewingSession`); that is expected. `EndedBySystem` with 0 attempts means the system never reported the document. To enable a read button only when a new read can begin at once, ask `CoreNfcChipRead.readiness()` and register `CoreNfcChipRead.addReadinessListener(listener)`; a start made earlier still works, it waits in `Starting`. iPhone has no signal for NFC switched off: that shows as `NotStarted` with `DISABLED`. `NOT_PERMITTED`, `NOT_ELIGIBLE` and `ACCESS_NOT_ANSWERED` are different setup problems; `ChipReadEnding.systemCode` holds Core NFC's code. A long read may pause for a moment with no update while it changes to a fresh connection to the document (`CoreNfcReadSettings.tagTimeLimitMillis`); that is expected.
- Read every ending of a chip read: `Complete`, `Partial`, `Failed`, `KeyNotAccepted`, `KeyRejected`, `Cancelled`, `EndedBySystem`, `NotStarted`. In a `when` on `ChipReadState`, five members are objects and seven are classes, so use `is` for the classes. Keep an `else` branch on endings: the sealed types may gain members.
- Never log chip files, the key, or an MRZ value. Error and observer text carries no document data by design.

Platforms are separate pages. A Kotlin page covers JVM and Android. A Swift page covers iOS. Do not mix their code.

## Common tasks

Read each list in order. Where no tutorial is named, none exists.

- Show the ready-made scanner screen. Android: [Read your first MRZ on Android with the ready-made screen](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-76), [Show the scanner screen on Android](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-74), [Theme the Android scanner screen](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-100). iOS: [Read your first MRZ on iOS with the ready-made screen](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-77), [Show the scanner screen on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-121), [Theme the iOS scanner screen](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-123).
- Scan with the camera behind your own UI. Android: [Read your first MRZ on Android with the headless camera](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-142), [Read an MRZ from the live camera on Android](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-14), [Show a live camera preview on Android](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-98). iOS: [Read your first MRZ on iOS with the headless camera](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-143), [Read an MRZ from the live camera on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-18), [Show a live camera preview on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-120).
- Parse an MRZ string. JVM and Kotlin: [Read your first MRZ on the JVM](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-10), [Parse an MRZ in Kotlin](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-25), [Read fields and dates from a parsed MRZ in Kotlin](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-33). iOS: [Install Tessera on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-110), [Parse an MRZ string on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-113), [Read fields and dates from a parsed MRZ on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-115).
- Read an MRZ from a saved photo. Android: [Read an MRZ from a saved image on Android](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-64), [Read capture metadata from a saved image on Android](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-95). iOS: [Read an MRZ from a saved image on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-116), [Read capture metadata from a saved image on iOS](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-114).
- Generate test MRZ data. Kotlin: [Read your first MRZ on the JVM](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-10), [Generate an MRZ in Kotlin](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-26), [Validate an MRZ in Kotlin](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-32).

## What works on which platform

✓ yes, ◐ partial, ✗ no, n/a not applicable. Details: [Capability matrix](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-139).

| Capability | JVM | Android | iOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parse and read fields | ✓ | ✓ | ◐ |
| Validate and check digits | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Look up codes and layouts | ✓ | ✓ | ◐ |
| Generate an MRZ | ✓ | ✓ | ◐ |
| Transliterate names | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Live camera, no UI | n/a | ✓ | ◐ |
| Torch control, no UI | n/a | ✓ | ✗ |
| Focus on the MRZ guide | n/a | ✗ | ✓ |
| Analyze your own frames | ✓ | ✓ | ◐ |
| Saved image | ◐ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Ready-made scanner screen | n/a | ✓ | ✓ |
| Frame agreement setting | n/a | ✓ | ✗ |
| Diagnostic events | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Install and align versions | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

- [Reader, not oracle](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-5): why the SDK reports and never judges

- [Century inference](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-84): how two-digit years become dates
- [Lockstep versions and the BOM](https://lightine.youtrack.cloud/articles/TES-A-85): one version for every module
